newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends lower,Central Bank sets pace.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends lower,Central Bank sets pace.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended sharply down on Monday at 26.280 pesos to the dollar from 26.263, prompted by a change in the Central Bank's desired trading range, traders said.
At midsession, the Central Bank quoted bid and offer rates of 26.235 and 26.285 against the previous 26.22 and 26.27.
"Banks just followed suit," said a local bank dealer.
Dealers, however, said the Central Bank was forced to adjust its rates because of the big dollar demand by a large commercial bank.
"I think the Central Bank was paranoid. It didn't want to sell dollars," said another dealer.
Banks were surprised by the Central Bank's action since fundamentals point to a strong peso. Banks would rather sell their dollars because of the high overnight rates, they said.
"There were some banks who wanted to short their (dollar) positions because of the higher overnight rates," the same trader said.
Market volume fell to $130 million from $174.90 million.

On Tuesday, dealers said the peso would probably rally in view of high domestic interest rates. Dealers said some banks had started to beef up their positions to prepare for the expected seasonal tightness during the Christmas season.
Moreover, the same bank buying dollars heavily had already satisfied their requirements, one dealer said.
